content.thinking:
I'm looking at the io-shop account page failures: ZeroDivisionErrors started after the monthly-spend flag went on at 04:05, and errors kept going after Argus turned the flag off. Code-Fix has proposed PR #556 as a fix, and I still need to work out why the errors continued once the flag was off.

I'm checking whether the flag-off reached request evaluation, since the logs I read stop at 04:12 and the flag went off at 04:12. I'm also tracing the causal chain from the failing account pages down to the flag switch at 04:05, ruling out deploys because none came back.

I'm checking whether any deploy landed in the change events I read: none came back, citing T9 and T28. I can't be sure the revision running on all three replicas was in place before the onset, though, so I'm keeping that claim modest.

I'm pinning down the causal step: turning on the monthly-spend flag made the account page call average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides by the count of this month's purchases, so a shopper with no purchases this month hits a zero divisor. That step rests only on the code reading F1, though the ZeroDivisionError at line 47 in G5309 fits it, so I'm treating the empty-list link as not yet independently confirmed.

I'm working out the root cause now: the monthly spend average divides by the count of this month's purchases with no empty-list check, so a shopper with no purchases this month triggers the ZeroDivisionError once the flag routes them there. The fault rests on that code path reading, which I haven't run, so I'm keeping that link open. The flag was ON at the end, so the failures could continue for those shoppers until it's turned off.

I'm looking at the contributing factors now: nothing in the pre-enable checks exercised the monthly path for a shopper with no purchases this month, and the flag went to full traffic at once rather than rolling out gradually.

I'm weighing whether the flag being off mattered for the incident response, and I'm noting that nobody was paged, so a person didn't get pulled in early to review the fix. I also want to record that the monthly-spend flag went to nearly all traffic at once, with no staged rollout, which made the blast radius larger.

I'm checking whether the flag revert actually stopped the harm, and I'm noting that the logs I read stop at 04:12, so they don't show whether requests evaluated the flag as off afterward. The flag was switched back on at P3 while the revert seemed not to help, which put back the path the logs link to the errors.

I'm checking whether the flag revert at T18 was judged fairly, since the verdict was based on the service at T20 without any record of requests evaluating the flag as off. I'm also noting that the second investigation landed on the same flag move already refuted, so it added nothing new.

I'm now checking how the response is credited: the Investigator's candidate at T13 named the monthly-spend switch and the division-by-zero error, Argus reverted the flag at T18, and Code-Fix proposed draft pull request #556 with tests at T37.

I'm checking what would actually stop the harm: the record shows that with the monthly-spend flag off, the ZeroDivisionError stopped and the error rate came back down, so I'm weighing whether switching it off again, and confirming that requests evaluate it as off, is the step that ends the failures.

I'm checking whether switching the monthly-spend flag off at P2 actually reached the replicas' per-request evaluation. I'm reading io-shop's evaluation log lines from 04:12 onward, and how rollout.py evaluates the monthly summary, to see whether requests kept treating it as on.

I'm drafting the action items now: one to roll out flags like monthly-spend-feature in stages with a small share of shoppers first, and one to require tests that run the flag-on path, including a shopper with no purchases this month, before a flag goes on in production. I'm also setting up a third to link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so someone gets paged.

I'm getting the assumptions down now: Code-Fix's reading is taken to describe the revision that was actually running on the replicas, since the deployment history never named it, and the shoppers whose pages failed are taken to be those with no purchases this month.

I'm noting that the logs I read stop at 04:12, so I can't see whether the flag was evaluated as off after the revert. I'm also ruling out other flag changes in the hour before the onset, since only Argus's switch shows up, and no deploy came back from the change events for the day before.

I'm drafting the causal chain now, starting with the account page failures and the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, both tied to the flag change at the onset. I'm checking which flag change lines up with the onset and whether any other change landed just before it.

I'm checking the causal chain's fourth step now: the flag being on routes shoppers into average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides by this month's purchase count, so a shopper with purchases before but none this month gets a zero divisor and a failed page.

I'm checking the symptom wording against the spec: account pages failed for shoppers, the ZeroDivisionError sits at the spend summary, and the monthly-spend flag is what routed those requests there. I'm dropping any specific figures and keeping the causal chain to one sentence at its last step.

I'm settling on how to name the affected code without a line number, and I'm keeping the error described as the ZeroDivisionError it raises. I'm also checking that the wording stays free of number words, and I'm making sure the phrasing about the shoppers and the timing starts from who did the work.

action_items.item: Turn on io-shop feature flags in stages: a small share of shoppers first, held at each stage while the account page error rate is watched, and rolled back automatically if it rises.

Before any io-shop feature flag can be switched on in production, require tests that run the code paths it enables with the flag on, covering ordinary account states such as a shopper with no purchases this month.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service's share of failed requests rose far above its usual level.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. This error first appears in the minute of the onset and does not appear before it.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: none came back from the production change events read for the day before the onset.
Another flag change: the flag provider showed no flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read except this switch of monthly-spend-feature.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests started taking the monthly spend path. An admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}, and from that minute the service's per-request evaluations of the flag read on. Before that they read off, and account pages rendered normally.

With the flag on, the account page works out each shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing by the number of purchases they made this month, and that raises ZeroDivisionError for every shopper who has bought nothing this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary on the account page sent shoppers through a calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought nothing this month, so their account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: monthly-spend-feature went from off to on for nearly all account page requests at the same moment. No staged rollout to a small share of shoppers was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout would have exposed only a small share of shoppers to the failing path while the rise in account page errors showed, which would have kept the harm much smaller.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for an ordinary account state such as a shopper with no purchases this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a check would have hit the ZeroDivisionError before the flag reached shoppers, and the flag would not have been switched on.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person paged when the alert fired would have been on hand to switch the flag back off, or to review the proposed fix, once Argus escalated. That would have shortened the incident.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent formed a candidate tying the failures to the switch-on of monthly-spend-feature and the ZeroDivisionError on account pages, and checked that no deploy was involved.
The Mitigation Agent tried a reversible action first, switching monthly-spend-feature off.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix with tests as a draft pull request, leaving it for a person to review.

went_wrong: When switching the flag off did not seem to help, the flag was put back on. That left on the path the logs tie to the failures, and the harm kept going.
The second investigation came back with the same candidate as the first, which had already been tested for C1 and judged refuted. It offered nothing new to try.

input.root_cause: In src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` integer-divides the account's spend this month by the count of purchases flagged `in_current_month`, with no check for an empty list. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, it raises ZeroDivisionError. `render_spend_summary` calls it whenever `use_monthly_summary` is true, and the request boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns the error into a failed account page.
input.still_at_risk: While monthly-spend-feature stayed on, account pages could keep failing for shoppers with no purchases this month, and the same failure could come back any time the flag is switched on before the fix is in.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at the service that io-shop's log lines show requests evaluating the flag off, that the ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stops appearing, and that the account page error rate returns to its level before the incident.
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out whether switching monthly-spend-feature off reached io-shop's per-request evaluation of the flag. Read the service's monthly-spend-feature evaluation log lines from the switch-off onward, and how src/io_shop/rollout.py turns the flag into `use_monthly_summary`, for example whether it caches the value. If requests did evaluate the flag off, find out why account page failures continued.
